A local minimizer of a differentiable function on an open interval
is a [flat point](calculus.qmd#def-flat-point),
and, at a flat point, a positive [second derivative](calculus.qmd#def-second-derivative) guarantees a strict local minimum.
This section extends both facts to a function $f$ of a $p \times 1$ vector $\vx$:
the gradient $\deriv{\vx} f(\vx)$ ([gradient](vector-calculus.qmd#def-vector-derivative)) takes the place of the first derivative,
and a $p \times p$ matrix of second partial derivatives takes the place of the second;
both facts are proved in this section, for every $p \ge 1$.
Throughout, $\deriv{\vx} f(\vecf{z})$ means the gradient evaluated at $\vx = \vecf{z}$.
